# Find the Town Judge.

@example Resident 2 trusts no one, and 1, 3 and 4 all trust 2. That 1 also trusts 3 changes nothing.
4
[[1,2],[3,2],[4,2],[1,3]]
=> 2

@example Resident 2 trusts no one, but resident 3 doesn't trust 2; 1 and 3 each trust somebody.
3
[[1,2],[3,1]]
=> -1

@example One resident and no pairs: that resident is the judge.
1
[]
=> 1

# Two residents and no pairs: nobody is trusted.
2
[]
=> -1

# Two residents who trust each other.
2
[[1,2],[2,1]]
=> -1

# Trusted by all four others, but trusts person 3 back.
5
[[1,5],[2,5],[3,5],[4,5],[5,3]]
=> -1

# Residents 4 and 5 trust no one, and neither is trusted by everyone else.
5
[[1,4],[2,4],[3,5],[1,2]]
=> -1

# The judge is person 1; the others also trust each other.
4
[[2,1],[3,1],[4,1],[2,3],[3,2],[4,3]]
=> 1

# The judge is person n, and every pair among the others is there both ways.
4
[[1,2],[2,1],[1,3],[3,1],[2,3],[3,2],[1,4],[2,4],[3,4]]
=> 4

# Random small cases from gen.c (lc check --regen makes them).
@gen 1 small
3
[[1,2],[2,3],[3,2],[1,3],[3,1]]
=> -1

@gen 2 small
5
[[5,1],[2,3],[4,3],[1,3],[5,3],[2,1],[4,1]]
=> 3

@gen 3 small
6
[[2,3],[1,3],[6,3],[3,2],[5,3],[2,4],[4,3]]
=> -1

@gen 11 small
5
[[2,3],[1,3],[3,4],[1,2],[2,4],[3,1],[5,2],[5,4],[1,4]]
=> 4

@gen 5 small
4
[[1,2],[4,2],[4,3],[1,4]]
=> -1

@gen 6 small
4
[[4,3],[1,3],[4,1]]
=> -1
